plugins.name: Beverage Finder by Taps + Tables
plugins.author: BevFinder
plugins.short_description: Beer and beverage finder that helps breweries, wineries, distilleries, and beverage brands show customers where to buy their products.
plugins.description:
Beverage Finder is a beer finder, beverage finder, and store locator for breweries, wineries, distilleries, and beverage brands. Show customers where to buy your products with an interactive map and searchable list of retail locations.

Features

  • Interactive Google Map with a sortable list of nearby locations
  • CSV import (works with Encompass sales reports or the included template)
  • Edit any location in the admin: name, address, products, and coordinates
  • Delete and restore locations one at a time, in bulk, or all at once
  • Setup checklist that shows exactly what’s left to do
  • Optional one-click address-to-coordinates lookup with a beveragefinder.net account
  • Download all of your locations as a CSV
  • Search by ZIP code and distance (10 to 250 miles, or any distance) — no API key needed
  • Brand/product filter
  • Visitor location via the browser’s built-in geolocation (no API needed)
  • Custom map pin, optionally shown above the map
  • Drag a location’s pin to the exact spot on a map, and review addresses that were only placed approximately
  • Hide text from location and product names, like your brand name or distributor codes such as (CHS)
  • Location expiration based on last delivery date
  • Unlimited locations
  • Responsive and mobile friendly
  • Works great as a beer finder or product locator
  • Find your product at stores, bars, restaurants, or other retailer

How it works

Import a CSV that includes latitude and longitude for each location. Locations appear on the map immediately. Re-importing updates delivery dates and coordinates for existing retailer/brand combinations instead of creating duplicates.

Only have street addresses? You can look up coordinates yourself on Google Maps, fill them in with any geocoding tool and re-import, or connect an optional beveragefinder.net account and click Get Coordinates on the BevFinder → Get Lat / Long screen. The account is a paid service with a free starter plan. Everything else in the plugin works fully without it, and the plugin only contacts beveragefinder.net when you click one of its buttons.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Google Maps Platform to display the map, and — only if you choose to — to beveragefinder.net to convert addresses into coordinates.

Google Maps JavaScript API (Google LLC)

  • What it’s used for: rendering the interactive map, location markers, and the “your location” marker icon, and the pin editor in the admin.
  • When data is sent: every time a visitor views a page containing the [beverage_finder] shortcode, and when a site administrator opens the pin editor on BevFinder → Locations.
  • What is sent: your Maps API key, the page’s referring URL, the visitor’s IP address and browser details (as part of any request to Google), and the map coordinates being displayed.
  • Terms of Service: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

The visitor’s own location (if they allow it) or the ZIP code they type is sent only to your WordPress site to sort results by distance. ZIP codes are looked up in a file bundled with the plugin (US Census ZCTA Gazetteer, a public-domain US Government work), not sent to any outside service.

beveragefinder.net address lookup (Taps + Tables)

  • What it’s used for: converting the street addresses of your locations into latitude/longitude, and showing your plan’s usage. beveragefinder.net uses the US Census Geocoder, with the Google Geocoding API as a fallback.
  • When data is sent: only when a site administrator saves a beveragefinder.net WordPress API Key on BevFinder → Get Lat / Long and then clicks Get Coordinates or Check account. Nothing is sent automatically, on a schedule, or from the front end.
  • What is sent: the WordPress API Key, your site URL, the plugin version, and the street address, city, state, and ZIP of locations that have no coordinates (or whose Google-provided coordinates are more than 30 days old, which Google’s terms require be refreshed). Retailer names, products, and sales data are not sent.
  • Terms of Service: https://beveragefinder.net/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://beveragefinder.net/privacy

plugins.name: Treatment Finder by PatientPulse
plugins.author: patientpulse
plugins.short_description: Adds the PatientPulse treatment finder to your clinic website. Connect once. No visitor leaves undecided. Every enquiry arrives briefed.
plugins.description:
PatientPulse is a treatment finder for aesthetic clinics and medispas. A visitor tells it what they are worried about, it guides them to the treatments on your menu that fit, and the enquiry lands in your PatientPulse dashboard with the visitor’s concern, budget and timing already written up.

This plugin is the WordPress connector for the PatientPulse service. It does one thing: it loads your treatment finder on every page of your site, using a site key that PatientPulse issues to your clinic. Everything else (your treatment menu, the questions the finder asks, enquiries, emails, appearance, billing) lives in your PatientPulse dashboard at app.patientpulse.co.

How it works

  1. Install the plugin and go to Settings > Treatment Finder by PatientPulse.
  2. Click Connect to PatientPulse. You are taken to app.patientpulse.co, sign in as usual (or start a trial), and confirm this website.
  3. That is it. The plugin receives a site key for your clinic and loads the finder on every page. Nothing to paste.

Requires a PatientPulse account

The treatment finder is a paid subscription service with a free trial. The plugin is free and open source, but the finder only shows to visitors while your PatientPulse subscription is active. Pricing and terms are at https://patientpulse.co/.

Per-site display options

Optionally override the button position, launcher style, accent colour and button text for this site only. Add [treatment_finder_by_patientpulse_launcher] to any page to place an inline launcher.

Developers

  • treatment_finder_by_patientpulse_should_load filter: return false to hide the finder on specific requests.
  • treatment_finder_by_patientpulse_app_url filter: point the plugin at a different PatientPulse environment.
  • The front end prints one async script tag and makes no server-side requests.

External services

This plugin connects to the PatientPulse service (https://app.patientpulse.co), operated by PatientPulse. It is required for the plugin to do anything.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click Connect: your site address (home URL), a random one-time state value and the plugin version, so PatientPulse can issue a site key to your clinic. The site key is exchanged server-to-server and stored in your WordPress options.
  • Once a day (and when you open Settings > Treatment Finder by PatientPulse or click Check now): the site key, your site address and the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, so PatientPulse can confirm the licence is active.
  • On your public pages: the browser loads the treatment finder script from app.patientpulse.co with your clinic identifier. Anything a visitor types into the finder (their concern, preferences, contact details when they choose to leave them) is sent to your PatientPulse dashboard. The finder records that it was loaded on your site so the dashboard can show the install as live.
  • When you click Disconnect or delete the plugin: the site key, so PatientPulse can revoke it.

Nothing is sent to PatientPulse until you click Connect. No data is sent to any other third party by this plugin.

Terms of service: https://app.patientpulse.co/terms
Privacy policy: https://app.patientpulse.co/privacy

plugins.name: MatrixMap – Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Store Locator & World Maps
plugins.author: MatrixAddons
plugins.short_description: Maps that work without an API key: a visual map builder, a store locator with "near me" search, and clickable world and region maps.
plugins.description:
Live demo | Website | Features | Free vs Pro | MatrixMap Pro | Pricing | FAQ | Documentation | Support

MatrixMap puts maps on your site in minutes, with no API key, no account and no monthly bill. Build a map with a visual editor, add a store locator that finds the nearest locations, or colour a world or country map with your own data. Everything is keyboard and screen reader accessible, and nothing loads until a visitor needs it. See it on the MatrixMap website or try the live demo right in your browser.

Why MatrixMap?

  • Free where others charge: the store locator, 302 region maps (including every US county), CSV import and plugin importers are all in the free plugin, with no limits on maps, places or locations and no MatrixMap branding on your maps.
  • No API key, no billing account: maps and address search work the moment you activate the plugin.
  • Built for real sites: privacy-friendly loading, keyboard and screen-reader support, and a 2 KB loader that only runs on pages with a map.
  • Easy to switch: bring your maps and stores over from eight popular map and store locator plugins without editing a page.

Made for

Store and dealer locators, franchises and chains, restaurants and cafés, real estate and property listings, tours and travel routes, events and venues, service areas and sales territories, and data stories such as election results, sales by state or members by country.

Three kinds of map

See them in action on the MatrixMap website.

  • Maps with places. Search for an address or click the map to drop a pin, then add a title, text, a photo, a phone number and a link. Group places into categories that visitors can filter. Draw areas, routes and circles, or add a GPX, KML or GeoJSON file.
  • Store locator. Keep your stores, dealers or offices as locations, each with an address, contact details, opening hours and your own extra details (parking, languages, services…). Visitors search by address or postcode, with suggestions from your own locations as they type, or tap Use my location. They get the nearest locations with distances, “Open now” status and one-tap directions in Google Maps, Apple Maps or Waze. Add the Store Search box to your home page or header to send visitors straight to their results.
  • World and region maps — 302 of them, all free. The world, continents, US states and the counties of every US state, the regions of 200+ countries, and detailed maps: French departments, Italian and Spanish provinces, UK local authorities, German districts, Indian districts, Australian council areas, New Zealand districts, Canadian economic regions, Philippine provinces and the municipalities of every Mexican state. Click a region on the map to edit it, edit many at once, or paste a spreadsheet to make a data map with a legend. Regions can link to pages or open their details in a panel beside the map or a pop-up window. Region maps load no map tiles and use no third-party services.
  • Region maps your way: colour each region or colour by value, bubbles, labels, groups, lines between places, pins or dots or your own icons with names beside them, start zoomed in on the regions you choose, limit the zoom, tooltips on hover or on click, and fade or hide regions without data.

Built around location

  • Near me: visitors share their location once and get the nearest results and directions from where they are.
  • Approximate location without asking: if your site is behind Cloudflare, CloudFront, Vercel, Fastly or Akamai, the locator can start near the visitor’s city using the country and city those networks already send. No prompt, no IP database, no extra service.
  • Smart address search: results favour the country your visitor is in and the countries where you have locations, and “Did you mean…?” suggestions help with ambiguous places.
  • Fast radius search from its own location index, even with thousands of locations.
  • Correct opening hours everywhere: each location’s time zone is worked out from where it is, so “Open now” is right for every branch.

No API key needed

Maps use free OpenStreetMap-based map styles (from OpenFreeMap) out of the box. You can switch to other free styles (topographic, cycling, public transport, satellite imagery), or add a key for Google Maps, MapTiler, Thunderforest or Mapbox if you prefer.

Privacy, speed and accessibility

  • GDPR-friendly loading: with a consent plugin (WP Consent API, Complianz, Cookiebot, CookieYes, Borlabs, iubenda), maps wait for consent. Visitors can also load a single map with one click.
  • Nothing on pages without a map. On pages with a map, a 2 KB loader waits until the map scrolls into view and then loads only what that map needs.
  • Accessible: markers are real buttons, popups can be used with the keyboard, and each map comes with a text list of its places. Region maps include a data table.
  • No scroll-jacking: on mobile the page scrolls normally and two fingers move the map; on desktop, Ctrl + scroll zooms.
  • Works with WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Perfmatters, SiteGround Optimizer, Autoptimize and FlyingPress.

Made for the block editor

Start from a ready-made template (one location, places with a list, a route, a store locator, countries you serve, a data map) or a blank map. The Map, Store Locator, Region Map and Store Search blocks show a live preview in the editor, and you can create or edit a map without leaving the page. Shortcodes and a classic widget work too.

Switching from another map plugin?

  • Popup text with simple formatting (bold, italic, links, lists)

  • Special opening hours (holidays) and temporary closures
  • Map styles, marker colours, icons and your own marker images
  • Full-screen button, “show my location” button and scale bar
  • Category legend, popup layouts, builder undo/redo and one-click sample data
  • Locator radius circle, sorting, “Copy link” and short ?near= links

  • Over 50,000 locations: only the visible area loads; resumable CSV imports

MatrixMap Pro

Everything above is free, with no limits on maps, places or locations. MatrixMap Pro is an optional add-on for businesses that want their maps to bring in customers. It adds:

  • Directions on your own map – driving, walking and cycling routes drawn on the map with travel time and turn-by-turn steps, from a locator result or a popup. Keyless routing (OSRM) or your own OpenRouteService, GraphHopper, Mapbox or Google key.
  • Locator analytics and a demand map – searches, directions, calls, website clicks and messages per location, and a map of where people search but you have no store. Anonymous, no cookies.

Upgrading from MatrixMaps 1.x

Your existing maps, [geo_maps] shortcodes and blocks keep working exactly where they are, with the same size, markers and popups. They are converted on the fly and your old settings are never deleted.

External services

MatrixMap connects to the services below only when a map, the store locator or an address search needs them. Region maps use none of them. No data is sent until a map is shown (and, with a consent plugin, until the visitor agrees). When a map is shown, the visitor’s browser downloads map images or data from the chosen provider, which receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details as with any web request.

OpenFreeMap (default map style)

Provides the default map styles, map tiles and map fonts from tiles.openfreemap.org. Used for every map unless you choose another style. The plugin’s Site Health check also requests one tile from your server to confirm the service is reachable. Service: https://openfreemap.org/ — map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

OpenStreetMap tile servers

If you choose the “OpenStreetMap” style or the plugin’s classic (Leaflet) engine, map images are loaded from tile.openstreetmap.org. Tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ — Privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Nominatim (default address search)

When you search an address in the map builder or location editor, or a visitor searches the store locator, the search text is sent from your server to nominatim.openstreetmap.org. Results are cached on your site. Usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ — Privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Photon (optional address search)

Only if you select Photon in Settings: search text is sent from your server to photon.komoot.io. Service: https://photon.komoot.io/ — Privacy policy: https://www.komoot.com/privacy

Optional free map styles

Only if you select them for a map:
* OpenTopoMap (tile.opentopomap.org): https://opentopomap.org/about
* CyclOSM (tile-cyclosm.openstreetmap.fr, hosted by OpenStreetMap France): https://www.cyclosm.org/
* ÖPNVKarte (tileserver.memomaps.de): https://memomaps.de/
* Esri World Imagery (server.arcgisonline.com): Terms https://www.esri.com/en-us/legal/terms/full-master-agreement — Privacy https://www.esri.com/en-us/privacy/overview

Google Maps Platform (optional, needs your API key)

Only if you add a Google API key: maps that use the Google engine load the Maps JavaScript API from maps.googleapis.com, and address search can use the Google Geocoding API from your server. The “Test key” button in Settings sends one Static Maps request. Terms: https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

MapTiler (optional, needs your API key)

Only if you add a MapTiler key and choose a MapTiler style or MapTiler address search: maps and searches use api.maptiler.com. Terms: https://www.maptiler.com/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://www.maptiler.com/privacy-policy/

Thunderforest (optional, needs your API key)

Only if you add a Thunderforest key and choose its style: map images load from tile.thunderforest.com. Terms: https://www.thunderforest.com/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://www.thunderforest.com/privacy/

Mapbox (optional, needs your access token)

Only if you add a Mapbox token and choose its style: map images load from api.mapbox.com. Terms: https://www.mapbox.com/legal/tos — Privacy policy: https://www.mapbox.com/legal/privacy

Directions links

“Directions” buttons are plain links to Google Maps (www.google.com/maps), Apple Maps (maps.apple.com) or Waze (waze.com) with the destination’s coordinates. Nothing is sent unless the visitor clicks one.

Source code

The readable JavaScript and SCSS source is in assets/src and is built with @wordpress/scripts (npm install && npm run build). The development repository is https://github.com/matrixaddons/geo-maps

Bundled libraries: MapLibre GL JS (BSD-3-Clause), Leaflet (BSD-2-Clause), Supercluster (ISC), d3-geo (ISC), @tmcw/togeojson (BSD-2-Clause) and Lucide icons (ISC). Region maps are built from Natural Earth data (public domain) and US Census county boundaries (public domain, via us-atlas, ISC). Detailed maps use open government data via geoBoundaries: Survey Department of Nepal / OCHA (CC BY 3.0 IGO), UK Office for National Statistics (Open Government Licence v3.0), © GeoBasis-DE / BKG (dl-de/by-2-0), Statistics Canada (Open Government Licence – Canada), Australian Bureau of Statistics (CC BY 4.0), Stats NZ (CC BY 4.0), World Bank / INEGI (CC BY 4.0) and lgdirectory.gov.in (ODbL). plugins.name: Treder Website Fix Finder
plugins.author: Ben Treder
plugins.short_description: Scan your WordPress site and get a clear, plain-English report showing what is hurting your trust, SEO, and conversions — with a prioritized fix list.
plugins.description:
Website Fix Finder runs a comprehensive audit of your WordPress site and produces a scored report in plain English — no technical jargon, no confusing dashboards. It shows you exactly what is wrong, why it matters, and how to fix it, in terms a business owner can act on immediately.

All checks run entirely on your server. No data is sent anywhere.

What It Checks

Website Fix Finder runs over 40 checks across 8 categories:

Website Basics
Site title, tagline, homepage type, HTTPS/SSL, clean permalink structure, search engine visibility, timezone, and language.

SEO Foundations
Homepage title quality, readable homepage content, H1 heading presence and count, number of published pages, descriptive page titles, image alt text, internal links, and SEO plugin/sitemap detection.

Trust Signals
Privacy policy page, contact page, about page, terms or disclaimer page, visible contact info on the homepage, and trust-building language.

Local Business Readiness
Local intent keywords, address or location information, Google Business Profile link, and LocalBusiness schema markup.

Mobile & User Clarity
Clear call to action, navigation menu, non-empty homepage, service or product pages, and shortcode clutter detection.

Content Quality
Placeholder text detection, default WordPress pages, homepage content depth, page variety (About / Services / Contact), and stale default posts.

Technical Health
PHP version, WordPress version, active theme, debug display visibility, Site URL / Home URL consistency, uploads directory writability, REST API accessibility, and WP Cron status.

Conversion Readiness
CTA phrases, contact path clarity, service/offer language, social proof, value proposition, and site-wide contact info.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Fix Finder in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  3. Click Run Website Scan.
  4. Review your Website Fix Score, top priority fixes, and full category-by-category breakdown.

Privacy

Website Fix Finder runs entirely on your server. No data is sent to any external service. Scan results are stored only in your WordPress database (wp_options) and are removed automatically when you uninstall the plugin.

Who Is This For?

  • Small business owners who built their own website and want an honest assessment
  • Freelancers and agencies who need a fast first-pass audit for client sites
  • Anyone who wants to improve their site’s trust, SEO, and conversions without hiring a consultant

Upgrade to Premium

Treder Website Fix Finder is useful on its own. Premium upgrade options may be offered separately from BenTreder.com for deeper scans, branded reports, scan history, client-friendly exports, and agency workflows.

Premium is optional. The free plugin works without a Premium purchase, account, or external service.

Premium features may include:

  • Multi-page scans
  • Branded PDF reports
  • Scan history and before/after tracking
  • Client report mode
  • WooCommerce checks
  • Local SEO expansion checks
  • Exportable issue lists

Learn more at BenTreder.com.

plugins.name: Groundwork Common Location Finder
plugins.author: groundworkcommon
plugins.short_description: A map-and-list location finder whose fields you define yourself. Only the name and coordinates are built in.
plugins.description:
Most location finders decide in advance what a location is: a store with a phone number, or a clinic with services. If your locations do not fit that shape, you end up storing “Wheelchair accessible” in a field labeled Fax.

This plugin has three built-in fields — name, latitude, longitude — and nothing else. Every other field is one you define in wp-admin: its type, its label, whether it shows on the result card or only in the detail pane, whether it is searchable, whether it becomes a filter. A food bank defines Services and Eligibility. A clinic defines Specialties and Languages Spoken. Neither pretends to be the other.

Field types

Nine simple types — text, textarea, URL, email, phone, number, yes/no, select, multi-select — plus three composites that are genuinely hard to do by hand:

  • Address — six subfields, a formatted one-line version, and a directions link.
  • Recurring hours — not just “9–5 Monday”, but “2nd and 4th Tuesday, 9am–4pm”. Consecutive days collapse on display, so seven rows read as “Mon–Fri 9am–5pm”.
  • Temporary closures — a date range with a reason. While one is active, the location shows a closure notice and stops reporting itself as open.

What visitors get

A map with pins and a list beside it, on one screen. Type to search; the typeahead suggests location names, cities, and the values of your own choice fields. Filter with chips. Press the crosshair button on the map to sort by distance from where you are — it is a sort, not a radius, so the nearest location is always shown even when it is 40 miles away. Selecting a location opens its details in place, without a page load.

It works without JavaScript, too: the page renders a plain list of locations that search engines can read and JavaScript replaces on boot.

Theming

The stylesheet ships structure, not opinions. Colors come from currentColor and the CSS system colors, so the finder inherits your theme’s palette, follows dark mode, and survives Windows High Contrast without configuration.

If you do want to color it, the Appearance tab has fifteen presets and twenty-five individual settings. Preset colors are all checked to WCAG AA contrast. Settings that override your theme do so with custom properties and no !important, so a theme that deliberately styles the finder still wins.

Privacy

The plugin sets no cookies, adds no tracking, and sends nothing about visitors to your server or anyone else’s. Location data stays in your database. The locate button reads the browser’s geolocation only after the visitor presses it, and the coordinates are used in the browser and never transmitted.

By default the map does not load until the visitor asks for it — see Ask before loading the map below. When they do, the choice is remembered in sessionStorage for that browsing session only. That is the one thing the plugin stores in a visitor’s browser: a single flag, never sent anywhere, gone when the tab closes.

See External services below for what does leave the site.

External services

This plugin relies on external services. Both are optional in the sense that they can be pointed elsewhere, but the defaults contact third parties, so here is exactly what is sent and when.

1. Map tiles — OpenStreetMap or CARTO

The map is drawn from tile images fetched by the visitor’s browser, directly from the tile provider. That means the provider receives the visitor’s IP address, user agent, and the map area being viewed. No other data is sent.

Because the request comes from the visitor rather than from your server, nothing server-side can prevent it once a map is on screen. So the plugin does not load tiles until the visitor asks it to. The map area shows a placeholder naming the provider and a Show map button, and no request reaches the provider until that button is pressed. The search, filters, location list and detail pane all work regardless — a visitor who never loads the map still gets a working finder.

This is on by default and can be turned off under Locations → Settings → Behavior (Ask before loading the map). It is skipped automatically when the tiles come from your own site, since there is no third party to ask about.

Which provider depends on the Map style setting under Locations → Settings → Appearance:

  • OpenStreetMap (default) — https://tile.openstreetmap.org
    Terms: OSMF tile usage policy
    Privacy: OSMF privacy policy
  • Light, Voyager, Dark — https://basemaps.cartocdn.com (CARTO)
    Terms: CARTO legal
    Privacy: CARTO privacy policy
    Note: CARTO’s free basemap tier is for non-commercial use. Commercial sites should use OpenStreetMap, or set a Custom tile URL for a provider they have an account with. The settings screen states this next to those three styles and again whenever one of them is the active choice.
  • Custom — whatever URL you enter. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

Attribution is a license condition, not decoration. The plugin prints the provider’s required attribution on the map and it must not be removed.

2. Address lookup — Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)

Used only in wp-admin, and only when a logged-in editor types into the address field of a location and asks for suggestions. The address text typed into that box is sent to https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search from your server, and the matching addresses and coordinates come back. Visitors never trigger it, and no visitor data is involved.

Nominatim’s usage policy requires an identifying contact address in the request, so the plugin sends the site URL and the contact email from Locations → Settings → Advanced (your admin email, by default). Requests are throttled to one per second per user.

Terms: OSMF Nominatim usage policy
Privacy: OSMF privacy policy

Not a service call: the Get directions link points at Google Maps or Apple Maps. It is an ordinary link — nothing is sent until a visitor clicks it, and then it is their browser making the request, not your site.

About Groundwork Common

This plugin is built and maintained by Groundwork Common, a technology practice for nonprofits: fractional technology leadership, project work, and training for organizations that need senior help and cannot carry a full-time technologist.

One of our working principles is that good technology work should leave an organization more capable, not more dependent on whoever did it. Releasing this plugin is that principle applied. A food bank or a clinic should be able to put its locations on a map without commissioning custom work or renting something this ordinary by the month.

If you find this plugin useful, three things genuinely help:

  • Recommend us. Mention us to a nonprofit who might benefit from our services. Referrals are how our business continues to grow its impact and reach.
  • Support our WordPress plugins directly. While we offer the plugin free to you, it costs us to maintain it — the security updates, the compatibility testing against each new WordPress release, the bug nobody but you has hit. We can’t do it without your support, and we appreciate whatever support you can give.
  • Report what broke. A clear bug report is worth more to us than most feature requests.

www.groundworkcommon.com

Third-party libraries

The plugin bundles one library and loads it from your own server. Nothing is fetched from a CDN, and there is no build step — every file the plugin ships is the file it runs.

Leaflet 1.9.4 — assets/leaflet/
License: BSD 2-Clause, included at assets/leaflet/LICENSE
Source: Leaflet 1.9.4 release

The bundled leaflet.js and leaflet.css are the official minified release files, byte for byte, with no modifications. The unminified source and the build tooling that produced them are at the URL above. The five PNGs under assets/leaflet/images/ are Leaflet’s own marker and layer sprites, under the same license.

All other code in this plugin is unminified and readable as shipped. The plugin’s own icons are inline SVG written directly in the source, not image files.
